summary: Two genuine one-click routes (OpenClaw, Hermes) on a normal VM, a manual route for everything else, and a separate per-session runtime for code interpreters and browser agents. DigitalOcean is not a good fit for the last two, because a Droplet bills by the hour it exists rather than by the work it does.

routes.what: The Marketplace 'Hermes Agent' image creates a Droplet with Hermes, Node and the OpenAI SDK installed. The listing publishes no post-deploy steps beyond the API example, so expect to add a model key and a channel in the console.
routes.disposition: Offer as a one-click route, flagged as partly no-terminal because the setup steps are unpublished.

routes.what: The hardened OpenClaw image provisions a Droplet with Caddy and a Let's Encrypt certificate, a generated gateway token, device pairing, container isolation, fail2ban and unattended upgrades. You still copy the gateway token and pair a device.
routes.disposition: Recommend. This is the cheapest hardened one-click OpenClaw here, and the only one that also gives a public IP and 16 regions.

routes.what: Install Claude Code or Codex on a Droplet yourself; the default images have no coding agent. A 2 vCPU / 4 GiB Basic Droplet at $24/month is enough for one developer.
routes.price: Up to $24/month for 2 vCPU / 4 GiB always on; less if it sleeps
routes.disposition: List as a manual route; no pick.

routes.what: Harness Runtime runs each session in a Firecracker microVM through doctl, PyDo or the API. Medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is $0.126 an hour at full allocation, with CPU and memory billed separately from storage.
routes.disposition: Backend route only. Do not price this with the Droplet card: it is a different product on a different meter, and the docs still bill 25% of allocated vCPU until active-CPU billing ships.

routes.what: Harness Runtime sessions include chromium and a browser-automation tool, but there is no desktop and no live preview of a running app.
routes.disposition: Backend route with a caveat; not a pick for computer-use agents.

routes.what: Run n8n and its database in Docker on one Droplet, keeping the encryption key yourself. A 2 vCPU / 4 GiB box at $24/month is the practical floor once the database is on the same machine.
routes.disposition: Manual route; no pick. No n8n image was verified in this research.

routes.what: An always-on Droplet keeps the Discord or Slack gateway connected, because nothing idles or stops it. 1 vCPU / 2 GiB at $12/month is enough for one server.

One Droplet per developer, each with its own login and credentials; there is no shared team login. Five 4 vCPU / 8 GiB boxes for eight hours a day over 20 days is 160 machine-hours each, and the 672-hour cap never binds at that rate.
routes.disposition: Manual route; no pick. The cap means a part-time box still costs the full month.

routes.what: cron inside a Droplet that stays on. DigitalOcean has no scheduler that starts a machine, so the idle hours between runs are billed at the full rate.
routes.disposition: Manual route; no pick. A task-per-run provider is cheaper for four runs a day.

routes.what: A small Droplet with a public IPv4 answers at a stable address all month. DigitalOcean's own MCP server manages DigitalOcean resources; it does not host your server.
routes.disposition: Recommend. Public IP, any TCP port, no idle stop, $6 a month.

picks.for: A cheap, hardened, always-on OpenClaw with its own public address
picks.why: A $12/month Droplet arrives with TLS, a gateway token, device pairing, container isolation and fail2ban already configured, on a real VM with root and 16 regions.
picks.watch: Powering off does not stop the bill, and the $12 tier is the floor only since the February 2026 update; the January image needed $24.

picks.for: A small always-on MCP endpoint on a known address
picks.why: $6 a month buys a 1 vCPU / 1 GiB Droplet with a public IPv4, any TCP port except SMTP, and no idle stop to wake from.
picks.watch: There is no hard spend cap and no tokenised URL: you add TLS and authentication yourself, and a spend alert only emails you.

notPicked.why: A Droplet bills for the hour it exists, not the work it does, so 1,000 ten-minute runs cost $10 and 1,000 hours of idling cost $24. Harness Runtime is the right DigitalOcean product here, and it is priced separately.
No desktop, no live preview and no per-session billing on a Droplet; Harness Runtime has chromium but is a backend product, not a computer-use desktop.
